title: Colours of light
examples: How does a rainbow happen with light?
Can I use a prism to see all the colours?
Is mixing colours the same as mixing light?

explain.say: White light is actually made up of many colours.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a prism splits light. Look at the white light, the prism and the refraction. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
When white light passes through a prism, it splits into its colours.
The order of the colours is always red to violet.
Mixing coloured paints creates new colours, but this is not like light.
When we mix light colours, we add the waves together.
In everyday life, a rainbow shows us this light splitting.

faq.q: Does every prism split white light into all colours?
faq.a: Yes, a prism is designed to separate white light into its component colours. It works because different colours bend at slightly different angles.
asks: What does a prism do to white light?
Can I use a prism to see the spectrum?

faq.q: Is mixing colours like mixing light?
faq.a: No, mixing paint is subtractive, meaning the pigments absorb light. Mixing light is additive, meaning the waves combine to make brighter colours.
asks: Does mixing paint make white light?
What is the difference between paint and light?

faq.q: What is the order of the colours in the spectrum?
faq.a: The colours appear in a specific order, starting with red on one side and ending with violet on the other. This order is always the same.
asks: Which colour is at the top of the rainbow?
Does the order of colours change?

faq.a: The visible spectrum is the small band of electromagnetic radiation that our eyes can detect. It includes all the colours from red to violet.
asks: What colours can our eyes see?
What is the range of visible light?

faq.q: Does the angle of the prism matter?
faq.a: Yes, the angle of the prism affects how much the light bends. A specific angle is needed to separate the colours clearly.
asks: How do I make the colours separate best?
Is the angle important for splitting light?

facts: White light contains all the colours of the visible spectrum.
A prism separates white light because different colours bend at different angles.
Mixing coloured paints is subtractive colour mixing.
Mixing primary light colours (red, green, blue) is additive.

quiz.say: When white light passes through a prism, what is the visible result?
quiz.why: The prism separates the single beam of white light into its component colours.

wrong.0: This is wrong because white light contains many colours, not just red.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the prism refracts the light, allowing us to see the colours.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the process separates the light into a range of colours.

quiz.say: If you mix red light and green light, what colour do you get?
quiz.why: In light, mixing red and green waves together creates the colour yellow.

wrong.0: This is wrong because mixing light waves does not create earthy colours like brown.
wrong.1: This is wrong because mixing primary colours always results in a visible colour.
wrong.2: This is wrong because red and green are primary light colours that combine.

quiz.say: What process describes mixing coloured paints?
quiz.why: Paint pigments absorb certain wavelengths of light, which is called subtractive mixing.

wrong.0: This is wrong because dispersion is the splitting of white light, not the mixing of pigments.
wrong.2: This is wrong because additive mixing applies only to light waves, not physical paints.
wrong.3: This is wrong because refraction is the bending of light by a medium, not the mixing of colours.
